The trail is a very beautiful, forested trail with dirt, rocks and some gravel in places. There were also some stairways made from rocks and what looked like railroad ties. There were a fair number of hikers on the trail including couples, small groups, and a few families (estimate approx. 150).  Lots of trees, plants and small animals e.g. chipmunks squirrels, even a racoon and possum on the return hike. The round trip hike on the trail to the valley below, including photo stops at look outs, took about 3 hours (estimated 15,807 steps per my Fitbit). Even though the major lookouts in and around the canyon below are well protected, some parts of the trail are near extremely high drop offs into the valley below. Extreme care should be given to any family's walking those parts of the trail with children.

This trail is a good challenge, lots of elevation changes. You’re climbing for a good chunk of it so wear good shoes. It’s well marked and can be crowded on the weekend. We had our two dogs and it was fine for them. Waterfall was a nice end point.

If you start at the top, and walk around residential area from Webster Falls to Tew’s Falls then you can walk down to Dundas Peak. We kept walking as there are no signs to stop. We went to Sydenham Falls and turned to go back deciding that Lookout is too further out. Again, no signs along the railroad that trail is closed. You then turn away from railroad going alongside the creek. 
At the end, when you make it back to Webster Falls, and you think you are short walk back up to the parking lot, you are in for a surprise:) 

You have to turn back. The steps to go up, do not exist. You are staring at the steep wall. You would have to climb the steep rocks, which is probably illegal,  and you would have to also climb over the fence!!! Do not do that. Very dangerous!!! 

The whole trail is very confusing, as it is unclear which parts of trail are open for hiking, which are not (like along the railroad, you don’t have to cross it, just walk along it, some resources say it’s illegal to cross, which I get, but is it illegal to walk alongside it?) I think the authorities need to make clear markings and put signs. It would be great to have a sign at the spot that leads away from railroad back towards Webster Falls with warning that it’s one way walk. Some resources say that it is illegal to hike  at the bottom of the Webster Falls, and there are no signs to indicate that. There are foot prints, the trail map shows where to go, so, we are not sure what is happening with this trail:( I would not go back.
